result.title: Sprint interval training improves HbA1c and insulin sensitivity in adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
result.abstractText: Adults with type 2 diabetes were randomized to sprint interval training or moderate continuous training for 10 weeks. Sprint interval training reduced HbA1c and improved insulin sensitivity compared with moderate continuous training.

result.title: Aerobic exercise and glucose handling in people with type 2 diabetes
result.abstractText: We examined 16 weeks of moderate aerobic exercise in people with type 2 diabetes. Fasting glucose improved modestly and medication use was unchanged.

result.title: Interval training in adults with type 2 diabetes: a pilot study of glycemic control
result.abstractText: Twelve adults with type 2 diabetes completed 6 weeks of interval training. Glycemic control tended to improve, but the study was not powered for definitive conclusions.

result.title: Effects of high-intensity interval training on glycemic control in type 2 diabetes: a randomized trial
Dietary polyphenols and glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes: a randomized crossover trial
result.abstractText: Adults with type 2 diabetes received a polyphenol-rich dietary supplement or placebo for 8 weeks in a randomized crossover design. Glycemic control and fasting glucose were assessed at baseline and follow-up.
